newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen falling as IMF aid ruled out.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen falling as IMF aid ruled out.

text.p: Thai stocks are seen moving lower on Friday as Thai officials ruled out a Japanese-backed or a IMF bailout package for the time being and risk sensitive investors sell ahead of a long weekend, analysts said.
The SET Index finished 7.38 points lower to 656.28 points on Thursday. The SET 50 eased 0.68 points to 49.68.
"It was wishful thinking on the part of some parties in the market, so I think we can expect a bit of profit taking," said Philip Adkins, head of research at Nava SC.

Thai Finance Thanong Bidaya and Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond have been in talks with their Japanese counterparts this week, but have said there will be no financial package for the ailing economy at this stage.

"I still think it will happen, it is a matter of timing but they want to do it on their terms which is understandable ... It is not the same as Mexico, Thailand is not in as bad a way as people think," Adkins said.
Police raids on two foreign brokerages suspected of spreading damaging rumours about the banking sector would have little bearing on the market, traders said.
